newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: DETAILS OF SLOVAK CORPORATE REVITALISATION DRAFT LAW.
newsitem.headline: DETAILS OF SLOVAK CORPORATE REVITALISATION DRAFT LAW.

text.p: The following are the main points of the Slovak government's draft law on corporate revitalisation, expected to be proposed at the next session of parliament in March.
The draft, made available to Reuters, sets out criteria and strategies of the government aimed at boosting the economic potential of selected Slovak companies.
**FORMS OF REVITALISATION**
-- Methods of easing debt range from debt deferment to relief, or a combination of the two.
-- The law also allows for the possibility of offering debt/equity repayment on condition that the bank will sell off the acquired shares within two years of the programme ending.
-- Debt relief options apply only to corporate debt accumulated up to the end of 1996.
**REVITALISATION COMMITTEE**

-- The law allows for the creation of a committee including the ministers of finance, economy, agriculture, social affairs and construction and the heads of the central bank (NBS), Slovenska Sporitelna, VUB Bank, IRB Bank and Slovenska Poistovna that will choose from applicants for the programme.
-- The committee determines the form of the revitalisation programme, its course or cancellation.
-- Committee decisions are irrevocable and lie outside legal jurisdiction and are binding for the individual ministries dealing with the applicants.

-- The committee will appoint a commissioner for each firm in the programme. This person will participate at the firm's board meetings and in fundamental financial or business decisions, and will report their findings to the committee.
**CRITERIA FOR APPLICATION**
-- Applicant firms must aim to secure employment in the region they are located, secure economic development in underdeveloped areas or develop economically important activities and fields.
**REVITALISATION OBLIGATIONS**
-- The law sets out a maximum term of three years for a firm in the revitalisation programme.
-- A firm in the prgramme cannot file for bankruptcy or be placed under bankruptcy during this period.
-- It must not pay dividends during the period, and must re-invest all profits.
-- It must accept certain limits, mainly in its asset mangement, and pay fines for not fulfilling the limits.
-- It must register all its obligations at separate subsidiary accounts, cannot waive its receivables.
-- It must present corporate information semi-annually and an audited balance sheet annually to its governing ministry for review.
-- If a revitalisation project is cancelled, the firm must repay all original obligations and those related to revitalisation.
-- The firm must pay a salary to its commissioner.
**TERMS OF REVITALISATION
-- There is no legal right for revitalisation.
-- There is no right to appeal against rejection or cancellation of a revitalisation programme.
-- All participants are under an oath of silence during the course of, and one year after, revitalisation is completed.
-- The start and end of a firm's revitalisation is registered at the commerce registry by their commissioners.
**FINANCING OF REVITALISATION
-- An amendment to the income tax law will create funding sources for revitalisation.
-- A revitalised firm obtains funds for the programme by exclusion of its debt write-off from a tax base.
-- A bank obtains the funds by acknowledging its write-off costs from a revitalised firm's debt as tax costs.
**APPLICATION FOR REVITALISATION**
-- Any Slovak firm in an unfavourable situation, which meets at least one of the criteria may apply by the year 2000 for revitalisation at a corresponding ministry.

-- The application must say which criteria is met, include an actual revitalisation project proposal, an audited balance sheet from the previous year and a list of debtors, creditors and outstanding debt.

-- It must include an obligatory statement by the firm's creditors and a financing bank on their opinion of the revitalisation proposal, and a confirmation that bankruptcy proceedings have not been filed.
-- Tatiana Vacova, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-521-8402
